rv.q: ROTHSCHILD & SONS is that rare Bock and Harnick musical that never seems to find its heart.
It does not, though, fix -- or "reimagine" -- the show.
Still, even a smoothly professional production can’t hide the doldrums that eventually set in with a disappointingly bland score...
Where the show falls down is in the music.
A show well worth seeing for the talent in the production, as well as for the history lesson to be learned on the Rothschild family.
In its present form, under the direction of Jeffrey B. Moss, it’s never less than absorbing.
I can only wish them well in finding a new life for it with this version.

It is this hokum, the cloyingly sentimental portrayal of some sort of do-gooder banking — financiers sans frontiers! — that undercuts the more successful parts of “Rothschild & Sons,” notably Bock’s melodies...
